messages.content: Hello, I'm ready to begin the interview.

I'm your technical interviewer for the Senior ML Engineer role at Streamside Media. I'll ask three distinct technical questions covering different aspects of production ML systems.

Question 1: Your NORDIC-ML paper touches on point-in-time correctness in feature pipelines. Walk me through a specific scenario where you had to choose between real-time feature computation versus pre-computed batch features for a ranking or recommendation system. What were the trade-offs in latency, freshness, staleness risk, and operational complexity, and how did you decide which approach to use?

In my last role I replaced a GBDT ranker with a two-tower retrieval model plus a LightGBM re-ranker. The two-tower gave us cheap candidate generation via approximate nearest neighbours, and the re-ranker kept feature-rich precision at the top of the list. We validated offline with NDCG on counterfactual replay of logged impressions before any online test, because naive offline metrics on logged data are biased toward the old policy.

response: Following up on that — when you moved to the two-tower plus re-ranker stack, the retrieval tower needed embedding lookups that had to be fast enough for your 90ms p99 latency target. Did you pre-compute and cache those embeddings, or compute them on-demand? And if you cached, how did you handle the freshness versus staleness trade-off when user or item behavior shifted?
